title: What would you rate this combat
author: YuukiCrypto
selftext:
I am planning on releasing a full combat trailer soon so would love to hear what you think about the combat on a scale from 1 to 10 - with 10 being the best.

  
Models and animations are still being worked on. I am more focused on game feel and how fun it feels without the animations and models being 10/10. I have experience with modeling, rigging, and animation. It will take several months to tweak the dashes, dodges, attack animations, etc

  
But in terms of a battle arena real time combat, how does this feel? How does the camera look? How do moves feel to hit? etc. 

I have changed a lot about the combat over the past few months so really trying to dial it in. I think I am close to what I imagine the final version to look like.

  
You can try it out here: [https://playkore.com/play/fuanara/](https://playkore.com/play/fuanara/)

comments.author: Aftermathrar
comments.body:
Specifically at 0:08-0:09, it wasn't clear if you meant to run into the ring of fire that killed you, or didn't see it and rolled that direction. I think it might be useful for these active AoEs to paint larger circle textures on the ground that fade, giving an off-camera effect another few meters of warning so that the player doesn't accidentally move into it. The circle texture's wouldn't be like your ground warning, but rather another layer to the move VFX so it's not as immediately obvious as the red indicator.

At 0:14 and elsewhere, your indicator width should very exactly match the width of the attack. Visually, it didn't look like those projectiles hit, but it seems like you got hit for 3 damage near the end of that sequence?  
At 0:16 there's a disconnect between the indicator ending and the damage arriving, even though you were point blank? The projectile was also not visible at any point except the end of the path?

Is the angle velocity rotation different between different creatures? Having an unresponsive turn radius seems like it would make the character feel pretty terrible to play (compared to only a slow walk speed). In that second fight, the indicators are a mess again and it's never clear exactly what is hitting who. Your creature should probably put down a (blue?) indicator of your own to assist lining up aoes.

It looks like you are trying to show off the iFrame mechanics with dodging, but the telegraphing to assist players with that is basically non-existent. Normally, the indicator would fill up like a progress bar to assist with timing of the dodge. Here, it seems to be relying on knowing the arbitrary timing?

At 0:50 when your character is losing, the ground indicators are gone and it's simply a mess of floating vfx. I would again suggest always having some sort of ground texture (or keep the indicator active in a slightly different shade) to make it clear where you will get damaged. This is especially true if these attacks were happening off screen and you were playing a fast-moving character like the frog or fox.

Are you really not able to move the camera around? The experience from 1:05-1:08 looked pretty annoying since the enemy was out of frame so often. The overhead view there and later are almost worse because of how close-up it is and it's not simply moving the camera overhead, it's changing the angle and moving overhead, so it's extra jarring.

comments.author: Janney1990
comments.body:
Looks horrible.

The models need walking/running animations so they don't look so clunky moving. They also need actual telegraphed animations for when a move is used that make sense.

IE; When the fox uses flamethrower it opens it's mouth and spews out fire.

Also looks janky af because none of the creatures are blinking or anything.

replies.author: YuukiCrypto
replies.body:
Noted. The actual "feel" of the game is great to me but animations and models are just as important. I understand that. It is one of the main reasons I was a little terrified to get into this genre. Oh well, only way to go from here and that is up. I already have running animations on things, the creatures were just not running (realized I had not done walking animations for all 260 fauna...)

As for the rest of the animations, yes of course I can work on polishing that up. Next post I make will have all the animations fleshed out. I've been mainly focused on the story, the open world, the MMORPG aspects, and proper progression systems

I updated the live game now so it defaults to sprinting, just like when you are not in battles. You can press shift to walk (or barely move analog). This is a super clean fix because i can just use the run animation but slowed down 

  
Thanks for the great feedback! Love this community
